title: Distribution ETF big-integer decoder rejects the u64-range positives its own encoder emits — round-trip and replay-file restore are broken for magnitudes in [2^63, 2^64-1]
purpose:
Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` finding M4 (reviewed at `fd71c5e`) — "Distribution big-integer decoder rejects `u64`-range positives its own encoder emits. `distribution/etf.rs:652` — `i64::try_from` fails for `SMALL_BIG_EXT` magnitudes in `[2^63, 2^64-1]` that `encode_big_bytes` produces; breaks round-trip and replay-file restore. The runtime decoder handles this correctly via `u128` + bigint fallback." Re-pinned at build base `a0359a2`.

RE-PIN. `crates/beamr/src/distribution/etf.rs` HAS drifted since the review commit (+8/-1 lines), but every change is below the defect: commit `3393b01` added the `mark_last_young_allocation_maybe_refcounted` call inside `alloc_binary_term` at `:735-745`. The M4 site is at `:652`, ABOVE that hunk, and is UNCHANGED. All line references below are current at `a0359a2` and were read at the bytes.

THE ENCODER. `encode_big_bytes` (`distribution/etf.rs:264-281`) trims trailing zero bytes off a little-endian magnitude (`:265-269`), then emits `SMALL_BIG_EXT` + a `u8` length when the trimmed magnitude is ≤ 255 bytes (`:270-272`) or `LARGE_BIG_EXT` + a `u32` length otherwise (`:273-277`), then a one-byte sign (`:278`), then the little-endian magnitude bytes (`:279`). It has two callers. `encode_i64_big` (`:246-250`) feeds it `value.unsigned_abs()` — for `i64::MIN` that is exactly 2^63, an 8-byte magnitude with sign=1. `encode_bigint` (`:252-261`) feeds it the concatenated little-endian limbs of a `BigInt` (`:257-260`) — for any single-limb `BigInt` whose limb is ≥ 2^63 and whose sign is POSITIVE, that is an 8-byte magnitude with sign=0.

THE DECODER. `decode_big_integer` (`distribution/etf.rs:634-672`), reached from both `SMALL_BIG_EXT` (`:569-572`) and `LARGE_BIG_EXT` (`:573-576`). For `len <= 8` (`:646`) it accumulates the magnitude into an `i128` (`:647-650`), applies the sign (`:651`), and then narrows: `let integer = i64::try_from(signed).map_err(|_| DecodeError::IntegerOutOfRange)?` at `:652`. The i128 accumulator makes the arithmetic itself safe; the `i64` NARROWING is the defect. Every positive magnitude in `[2^63, 2^64-1]` — the entire upper half of the u64 range, all of which the encoder emits as an 8-byte `SMALL_BIG_EXT` — fails that `try_from` and becomes `DecodeError::IntegerOutOfRange`. (The negative boundary survives by accident: `-2^63` narrows to `i64::MIN` exactly, so `i64::MIN` round-trips while `2^63` does not. That asymmetry is the tell that this is a narrowing bug and not a deliberate range policy.) The `len > 8` branch (`:659-671`) is correct — it builds `u64` limbs and calls `alloc_bigint_term` with no narrowing — so the defect is confined to the single-limb path.

THE MIRROR THE FIX MUST FOLLOW, CITED EXACTLY. The runtime ETF decoder solves the identical problem correctly: `crates/beamr/src/etf/decode.rs:433-490`, `decode_big_integer`. Same structure, same `len <= 8` fast path, but it accumulates into a `u128` at `:447-449` and then branches THREE ways instead of narrowing: (1) `value <= i64::MAX as u128` at `:451` → a small int if it fits (`:454-455`), else a single-limb bigint from `integer.unsigned_abs()` (`:456-461`); (2) `negative && value == (i64::MAX as u128) + 1` at `:462` → the `i64::MIN` boundary, allocated as a bigint carrying `i64::MIN.unsigned_abs()` (`:463-465`); (3) otherwise at `:466-470` → `u64::try_from(value)` (which cannot fail on this path, since `len <= 8` bounds `value` by `u64::MAX`, but is written fallibly rather than with a cast) and a single-limb bigint with the decoded sign. The runtime decoder ALSO already carries a pinning test for exactly the defective case: `crates/beamr/src/etf/decode.rs:683-705`, `small_big_ext_positive_above_i64_max_decodes_to_bigint`, which feeds a `SMALL_BIG_EXT` with magnitude `(i64::MAX as u64) + 1`, sign 0, and asserts the result is a non-negative `BigInt` with `limbs() == &[(i64::MAX as u64) + 1]`. That test is the shape of the wall this brief owes on the distribution side, and its existence is proof the correct behaviour was already understood in one half of the codebase and never propagated to the other.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND DISTRIBUTION — THE REPLAY PATH. `crates/beamr/src/replay/file.rs` is a consumer of this exact encoder/decoder pair, not of the runtime one: `:414` encodes via `crate::distribution::etf::encode_term_result`, `:426` decodes via `crate::distribution::etf::decode_term`, and `:34-35` wrap both error types into the replay error enum. So a process that ever holds an integer in `[2^63, 2^64-1]` writes a replay file that CANNOT BE RESTORED — the record is written successfully and fails only on read, which is the worst failure ordering available: the operator learns the log is unusable at the moment they need it. The distribution face is the symmetric one: a beamr node encodes such an integer, sends it, and the receiving beamr node refuses its own wire format. This is a self-incompatibility, not an interop gap.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided; no fork). The distribution decoder's single-limb path is brought to the runtime decoder's behaviour EXACTLY — same accumulator width, same three-way branch, same boundary handling — so that the two decoders agree by construction and can be diffed line-for-line by a reviewer. This is a mirror, not a redesign: no new error variant, no new tag support, no widening of what the ENCODER emits, no change to any wire byte.

D1 — MIRROR THE SINGLE-LIMB PATH. Replace `distribution/etf.rs:647-658` with the runtime decoder's shape from `etf/decode.rs:447-471`: accumulate into `u128` rather than `i128`; branch (a) `value <= i64::MAX as u128` → `Term::try_small_int` if it fits, else a single-limb bigint via `alloc_bigint_term(heap, negative, &[magnitude])`; branch (b) `negative && value == (i64::MAX as u128) + 1` → the `i64::MIN` boundary as a bigint carrying `i64::MIN.unsigned_abs()`; branch (c) otherwise → `u64::try_from(value)` into a single-limb bigint with the decoded sign. `DecodeError::IntegerOutOfRange` REMAINS in the enum and remains reachable — it is the honest error for a genuinely undecodable magnitude — but it must no longer fire for anything `encode_big_bytes` can emit. The two allocation seams differ and must not be conflated: the runtime decoder allocates through `ProcessContext::alloc_bigint`, the distribution decoder through the free function `alloc_bigint_term(heap, negative, &limbs)` (`distribution/etf.rs`, immediately after `alloc_binary_term`). Use the distribution seam; do not import the runtime one.

D2 — THE MIRROR IS PINNED AS A MIRROR. The comparison is the point, so it is walled and not merely done: the new distribution-side test carries a comment naming `crates/beamr/src/etf/decode.rs:433-490` as the authority it mirrors and `:683-705` as the runtime twin of its own assertion, so that a future divergence in either decoder is visible to whoever next opens either file. This is documentation-as-wall, the same device `AUDIT.md`'s named-load-bearing-fact rider uses.

D3 — THE RED IS A ROUND-TRIP PROPERTY, NOT A CASE LIST. The requirement the review states is a PROPERTY: everything `encode_big_bytes` emits must decode back. A hand-picked case list would have missed this defect for the same reason the existing suite did — the boundary is not where anyone thinks to look, and the negative side round-trips while the positive side does not. R1 therefore builds a table-driven round-trip over the encoder's own output for a magnitude table that provably covers every structural boundary of `encode_big_bytes`: the small-int/bignum boundary either side, `i64::MAX`, `i64::MAX + 1`, `i64::MIN`, `2^63` positive (the defect's floor), `u64::MAX` (its ceiling), a value with trailing zero bytes in its magnitude (to exercise the trim at `:265-269`), a multi-limb `BigInt`, and a magnitude of exactly 256 bytes (the `SMALL_BIG_EXT` → `LARGE_BIG_EXT` crossover at `:270-277`) in both signs. The invariant asserted is not 'decodes without error' but 'decodes to a term EQUAL to the one encoded' — a decoder that returned the wrong bigint would pass the weaker form.

D4 — THE REPLAY LEG IS SEPARATE AND REQUIRED. The unit-level round-trip proves the codec; it does not prove the consumer. R3 adds a replay-file leg driving `replay/file.rs`'s real write-then-read path with a term in the defective range, because that is the failure the operator actually meets and because it is the leg that would catch a future re-routing of replay onto a different codec.

requirements.title: RED — encoder/decoder round-trip property over every structural boundary of `encode_big_bytes`
requirements.spec: Per D3: a table-driven round-trip test in `distribution/etf.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (at `:984`, house pattern — it already builds a `Heap::new(2048)` via the `heap()` helper and asserts on `encode_term` output byte vectors). For each entry: encode via the public `encode_term`/`encode_term_result` path, decode via `decode_term` into a fresh heap, and assert the decoded term EQUALS the encoded one (small ints by raw equality; bigints by sign and limbs, the shape `etf/decode.rs:704-705` uses). Table entries: `i64::MAX`, `i64::MAX - 1`, `i64::MIN`, `i64::MIN + 1`, `2^63` as a positive single-limb `BigInt`, `2^63 + 1`, `u64::MAX`, a positive single-limb value with trailing zero magnitude bytes, a multi-limb `BigInt` both signs, a magnitude of exactly 256 bytes both signs (the `SMALL_BIG_EXT`/`LARGE_BIG_EXT` crossover), and the small-int boundary either side. Must be RED at `a0359a2` on the positive `[2^63, 2^64-1]` entries with `DecodeError::IntegerOutOfRange` and GREEN on everything else — the split itself is evidence the table is discriminating rather than uniformly broken.
acceptance: RED at `a0359a2` on the `2^63`, `2^63 + 1` and `u64::MAX` positive entries, with the observed `IntegerOutOfRange` error recorded verbatim in the evidence run log; GREEN at `a0359a2` on `i64::MIN` (the asymmetry is asserted explicitly, with a comment, because it is the diagnostic that identifies this as a narrowing bug and not a range policy)
The assertion is term EQUALITY (sign + limbs, or raw small-int equality), not merely `is_ok()` — a decoder returning a wrong-but-well-formed bigint must fail this wall
The `LARGE_BIG_EXT` crossover entries are present and green both before and after, proving the `len > 8` path (`:659-671`) is untouched and that the fix did not migrate the defect across the branch
One minimal semantic mutation committed as a diff + observed red run under `docs/design/beamr/briefs/evidence/review-23-07/rf-008/mutations/` and `runs/`, never applied to the tree

requirements.title: GREEN — the single-limb path mirrors the runtime decoder
requirements.spec: Per D1 and D2: `decode_big_integer`'s `len <= 8` branch (`distribution/etf.rs:646-658`) is rewritten to the runtime decoder's three-way `u128` shape (`etf/decode.rs:447-471`), allocating through the distribution seam `alloc_bigint_term`. The `len > 8` branch is untouched. A comment on the rewritten branch names `crates/beamr/src/etf/decode.rs:433-490` as the authority it mirrors.
acceptance: R1 fully green; the two decoders' single-limb branches are structurally diffable — same accumulator width, same three branch conditions in the same order, same boundary constant

`DecodeError::IntegerOutOfRange` still exists and is still reachable for a genuinely undecodable input; a test pins that it is NOT reachable for any output of `encode_big_bytes` (this is the property R1 asserts, restated as the invariant this requirement preserves)

ZERO wire-format change: no encoder line is modified, and the existing `encodes_*` byte-vector assertions in the same test module pass unchanged with no edits — the artifact is the untouched-encoder half of `git diff`
Fail-first recorded: revert R2 → R1 red on the three positive u64-range entries → restore

requirements.title: The consumer leg — a replay file carrying a u64-range positive restores
requirements.spec: Per D4: a test driving `crates/beamr/src/replay/file.rs`'s real write-then-read path (the `crate::distribution::etf::encode_term_result` seam at `:414` and the `decode_term` seam at `:426`) with a term in `[2^63, 2^64-1]`, asserting the restored term equals the recorded one. Red at `a0359a2` — the write succeeds and the read fails with `ReplayError::DecodeTerm(IntegerOutOfRange)` (`:35`) — and green after R2.
acceptance: Red at `a0359a2` with the failure recorded at the READ, not the write — the observed error and the fact that the write reported success are both captured, because the write-succeeds/read-fails ordering is the operator-facing severity of this defect
Green after R2 with the restored term asserted EQUAL to the recorded term

The test drives the replay module's real public path; it does not reach into `distribution::etf` directly (that is R1's job) — the point of this leg is precisely that it would survive a re-routing of replay onto a different codec and would then be testing the new one

boundaries: PATH CONFIRMATION, stated explicitly as required: the file under repair is `crates/beamr/src/distribution/etf.rs`. It is NOT under `crates/beamr/src/loader/encode/**` — that directory contains `chunks.rs`, `code.rs`, `compact.rs`, `container.rs`, `literals.rs`, `mod.rs`, `opcodes.rs` and is the `.beam` WRITER, an entirely separate subsystem from the Erlang External Term Format codec. `loader/encode/**` is untouchable (Vesper Lynd's claim) and this brief touches no file under it. The unrelated third codec `crates/beamr/src/etf/` is READ ONLY in this brief: it is the correctness authority being mirrored, and modifying it would destroy the reference.

NO WIRE-FORMAT CHANGE. `encode_big_bytes` and both its callers are not modified. This brief widens what the decoder ACCEPTS to match what the encoder already EMITS; it does not change what is emitted. Any change to an encoder byte is a STOP — the wire format is an interop surface with real OTP nodes.

The `len > 8` multi-limb branch (`distribution/etf.rs:659-671`) is correct and is not modified. If the drafter believes it needs changing, that is a STOP and a separate finding, not a scope expansion.
No new `DecodeError` variant. `IntegerOutOfRange` is retained and remains reachable; the defect is that it fires where it must not, not that it exists.

ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` catch-all arms — note the decoder's tag dispatch already ends in a named `other => Err(DecodeError::UnsupportedTag(other))` at `:596`, which is a bound binding and not a catch-all, and it stays that way; NO-POLLING; no new knobs (no configurable integer range, no strict/lenient decode mode).
Both wasm32 check closures stay green; `crates/beamr-wasm/src/reasons.rs` needs no additive row because no `ExecError` variant is added.
verification: Full release battery on the final head: the 5 legs of `gates.json` (`fmt`; `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` fresh-lint with Compiling lines; `wasm32-check` locked; `wasm-tests`; `cargo test --workspace`), plus the prohibition greps (zero new `#[allow]`, zero `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`, zero new `_ =>`). Because this brief touches the distribution codec, the distribution integration legs are called out for explicit attention rather than left to the workspace run: `crates/beamr/tests/distribution_e2e.rs`, `distribution_mesh_handshake.rs`, `link_distribution_e2e.rs`, `pg_distribution_e2e.rs`, `encode_round_trip.rs` — all green and unedited. FAIL-FIRST REVERT DEMONSTRATION: revert R2 → R1 red on the three positive u64-range entries and R3 red at the restore → restore and re-run green, both runs logged. MUTATION EVIDENCE per R1: one minimal semantic mutation as a committed diff + observed red run, never applied to the tree. PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY at the actual build base before the first commit — re-read and re-record: `distribution/etf.rs:264-281` (`encode_big_bytes`), `:246-250` and `:252-261` (both callers), `:569-576` (both tag arms), `:634-672` (`decode_big_integer`, the defect at `:652`), `alloc_bigint_term`'s current definition and signature; `etf/decode.rs:433-490` (the mirror) and `:683-705` (the runtime twin test); `replay/file.rs:34-35`, `:414`, `:426`. Note that `distribution/etf.rs` already drifted +8/-1 between the review commit `fd71c5e` and `a0359a2` (commit `3393b01`, the `mark_last_young_allocation_maybe_refcounted` call in `alloc_binary_term` at `:735-745`, entirely below the defect) — if further drift has landed at the build base, re-derive line numbers before citing them in any comment. HANDOFF carries: the round-trip table as landed, the before/after `IntegerOutOfRange` reachability statement, confirmation that the encoder half of the diff is empty, and the `git diff --stat` proving `loader/encode/**` and `crates/beamr/src/etf/**` are untouched.
